text: The Valley of Clans. Long ago, the valley was full of brave clans. They dug for treasure, built bright villages, and stood together when trouble came.
The empty village. But the old clans scattered far and wide. Now one little village sits empty at the foot of the hills, waiting for someone new.
Four heroes. That someone is you. Gather four heroes, give your clan a name, and raise your banner over the village gate.
The glowing mines. Under the hills, the old mines still glow with gold and gems. Monsters live down there too. The deeper you go, the bigger they get.
Six kingdoms. From their hills, the six kingdoms watch your little village grow. Grow strong enough, and even Dragon's Rest will take notice.
Something wakes. And every season, deep in the mountains, something big wakes up. Build. Train. Be ready. The valley is counting on your clan!
Thunder in the hills. The sky turns purple. Thunder rolls over the hills, and the church bell starts to ring all by itself.
Grimmor wakes. High in the mountains, Grimmor the Storm Giant stretches, yawns, and picks up a boulder the size of a house.
To the walls! "He is coming this way!" shout the scouts. your clan, it is monster week. Every fight counts!
The last stand. Lightning cracks across the sky. Grimmor raises his great club one last time… but your clan stand firm at the gate.
The giant falls. One final blow! Grimmor stumbles, and crashes down onto his knees. The ground shakes so hard that the church bell rings.
The storm breaks. The thunder stops. The clouds part, and moonlight pours over the valley. Grimmor looks down at your clan… and smiles. "Brave little ones," he rumbles.
Back to the mountains. At dawn Grimmor leaves his great club at the village gate, and stomps away to the mountains. He will not trouble the village again.
The village cheers! Lanterns, music and a feast! The whole village cheers for your clan. Grimmor's club hangs over the gate, for everyone to see.
The ground shakes. Cups rattle on the tables. Dust drifts down from the roofs. Something heavy is walking under the hills.
Craghold wakes. A whole hillside stands up. It is Old Craghold the Stone Golem, with two glowing amber eyes.
To the walls! "He is rolling this way!" shout the scouts. your clan, it is monster week. Every fight counts!
The last stand. Dust swirls and the ground shakes. Craghold lifts both stone fists… but your clan stand firm at the gate.
The golem cracks. One final blow! A great crack runs down Craghold's chest, and the golem sinks onto one knee with a rumble like thunder.
The dust settles. The dust settles and the moon comes out. Craghold's amber eyes glow softly. "Strong little ones," he grinds, and he almost smiles.
Back to the hills. At dawn Craghold leaves his glowing stone heart at the village gate, and rolls slowly away to the far hills.
The village cheers! Lanterns, music and a feast! The whole village cheers for your clan. Craghold's stone heart glows over the gate, for everyone to see.
A cold wind. Snow falls in the middle of the day. The well freezes over, and every chicken hides under the hay.
Frostjaw wakes. From the far north comes Frostjaw the Ice Troll, sniffing the air and grinning a frosty grin.
To the walls! "He is stomping this way!" shout the scouts. your clan, it is monster week. Every fight counts!
The last stand. Snow howls through the village. Frostjaw takes one last icy breath… but your clan stand firm at the gate.
The troll slips. One final blow! Frostjaw skids on his own ice and crashes down in a huge cloud of snow.
The blizzard stops. The wind drops and the stars come out. Frostjaw shakes the snow off his fur and grins at your clan. "Tough little ones," he growls.
Back to the north. At dawn Frostjaw leaves one icy tooth at the village gate, and runs off to the far north, shivering.
The village cheers! Lanterns, music and a feast! The whole village cheers for your clan. Frostjaw's icy tooth sparkles over the gate, for everyone to see.
The last gems. At the top of Crystal Valley stands the Keep. Inside, the last magic gems glow, keeping the whole valley green and warm.
Warlord Mudtooth. Far over the hills, Warlord Mudtooth hears about the gems. He wants them all for his crown, so he calls his Grey Horde.
You are the Keeper. The old Keeper is ready to rest, and hands you the big iron key. "Build towers, set the gems, and keep the valley safe."
Scouts in the valley. Mudtooth's scouts are creeping up the valley to count your towers. Don't let a single one reach the Keep and run home to tell.
Dry hay. Every barn in the meadow is full of dry hay. One spark and it would all go up in flames. Keep the red fire gems out of your towers.
The wobbly bridge. The only bridge over the river is old and wobbly. Too many towers and it will tip into the water. Build no more than 8.
The blocked cave. A rockfall has blocked the cave where the blue frost crystals grow. You will have to win this one without any blue gems.
Hiding in the woods. Families from the villages are hiding in the woods beside the road. Let no more than 2 enemies past, so nobody finds them.
The drummers. Mudtooth's drummers bang on the Keep's wall as they march past. Keep the wall strong: finish with the Keep at 80 or more.
Frozen mushrooms. Up on Frost Ridge, the poison mushrooms are frozen solid, so the green gems have no power. Win without any green gems.
Wood for the gates. The gate-keepers need wood to fix the Twin Gates. Build no more than 11 towers, so there is plenty left over.
Lightning. Lightning crackles over the peaks. Yellow gems would pull it down onto your own towers. Leave the yellow gems out.
Mudtooth himself. Mudtooth himself has come, with every soldier he has left. The Keep's old wall is cracked. Finish with the Keep at 50 or more.
Nobody counted. Not one scout got home. Mudtooth stamps his foot. "How many towers? Nobody knows how many towers!"
Strawberries. The hay is safe. The farmers bring you a basket of strawberries and promise to ring the bell if the Horde comes back.
The otters help. The bridge still stands. The river otters patch it with sticks, and the Horde's rafts get stuck in the mud.
A secret note. The miners dig out the blue cave and find a note a soldier dropped. Mudtooth has a secret plan for the Two Rivers.
Safe and sound. The families come out of the woods, safe and sound, cheering. Their grandad gives you a horn to call them if you ever need help.
Drums down. The wall hardly has a scratch. The drummers look at each other, drop their drums, and walk home.
The mushrooms wake. Behind you the ice melts. The mushrooms wake up and sneeze green dust all over the Horde's backs. Achoo!
One road left. Spare wood mends both gates. Now only one road leads to the Keep, and Mudtooth is running out of soldiers.
Bonk! Bonk! The lightning finds the two bosses' tall metal helmets instead. Bonk! Bonk! They slide all the way down the mountain on their shields.
The wall holds. The cracked old wall holds. Mudtooth stares up at the Keep, still standing, its gems still glowing. He has nothing left to send.
Mudtooth gives up. Mudtooth sits down on a rock. "I'm tired," he says. "My feet hurt. And I don't even like gems that much."
Going home. The Grey Horde packs up and trudges home over the hills, grumbling. A few of them even wave goodbye.
The book of Keepers. The whole valley has a party. Your name goes into the big book of Keepers, and the gems glow brighter than ever.
A green storm. One quiet afternoon, a strange green storm rolled over Castle Fields. The clouds giggled. Clouds are not supposed to giggle.
Goblins! Then it started to rain goblins. Hundreds of them, with bats and slimes and a very big troll, all running for the castle.
The bell rings. Up in the tower, the castle bell rang out. Ding! Ding! Ding! It only rings for one thing: heroes, come quickly!
How long can you last? Pick up gems to grow stronger. Choose your powers. The Goblin King is coming at the end. How long can you last?
The last guard. When the goblins came, every guard ran away except one. The Knight just stood at the gate, folded their arms, and said, "No."
Grandma's blades. The Knight's grandmother guarded the castle first. On the Knight's first day, Grandma handed over two shining blades and one piece of advice: "Never run."
Spinning blades. Now the blades spin around the Knight like a shining shield. Slow, yes, but very, very hard to knock over.
From the Dark Forest. The Ranger grew up deep in the Dark Forest, where the trees are so tall that the sun only visits on Tuesdays.
Forest friends. The forest looks after its own. Leaves whirl, hawks dive and wasps sting whenever the Ranger is in trouble.
Arrows ready. Quick on their feet with a sharp eye, the Ranger can pull gems from far away. Goblins never see the arrows coming.
Oops. At wizard school, the Wizard once sneezed during a fire spell and set the whole library alight. Everyone still talks about it.
Practice, practice. So the Wizard practised every single day, until every fireball went exactly where it was pointed. Well, nearly every one.
Bigger spells. Now the Wizard's spells are bigger than anyone else's. Goblins have learned to keep away from the purple hat.
From the Frozen Peaks. The Barbarian comes from the Frozen Peaks, where people wrestle bears for fun and have snowball fights in blizzards.
Cross. He is very friendly, until somebody makes him cross. And the crosser he gets, the harder he hits.
Very cross. Goblins stole his lunch on the way here. He is now extremely cross. The goblins have made a big mistake.
The chapel. The Cleric looks after the little chapel by the old graveyard, polishing the bell and keeping the candles lit.
A helping hand. Anyone hurt finds their way to the chapel door, and the Cleric always helps. A scraped knee, a sore paw, a broken wing.
A ring of light. Now a ring of holy light goes with the Cleric into battle. It hurts goblins and slowly heals the Cleric as they go.
Just a joke. For a joke, the Rogue once sneaked into the goblin camp and swapped the Goblin King's crown for a saucepan.
Very angry goblins. The Goblin King did not think it was funny. Now every goblin in the land wants that crown back.
Too fast to catch. Lucky for the Rogue, nobody is faster. Shadows strike, goblins tumble, and the Rogue is already gone.
Up on the peaks. High on the coldest mountain lives the Frost Witch, with a family of fluffy snow owls who sit on her hat.
A cold welcome. She is kind, but very chilly. Anything that comes close to her starts to shiver and slow right down.
Frost rings. Rings of frost ripple out from her crystal wand. The owls think it is the best game ever.
A dragon. Really. Everyone says the Dragon Kid is just a kid in a dragon suit. The Dragon Kid says that is exactly what a dragon would want you to think.
Not a monster. The stories always make dragons the baddies. The Dragon Kid wants to be the first dragon who is a hero instead.
Hot breath. Tough scales, tiny wings, and fireballs that really work. The goblins are not laughing at the suit any more.
Into the Dark Forest. The storm has blown into the Dark Forest. The mushrooms are angry, the wolves are hungry, and somewhere a Forest Ogre is stomping about.
The Haunted Graveyard. Mist creeps between the old stones. Skeletons rattle, ghosts go "Wooo," and the Lich is waving its glowing staff.
The Frozen Peaks. Up where the snow never melts, yetis are throwing snowballs the size of sheep. High above, an Ice Dragon spreads its wings.
The Lava Mines. Deep under the mountain, the rocks glow red hot. The last of the storm is here, and so is the biggest boss of all: the Fire Dragon.
The Goblin King runs! The Goblin King drops his club, grabs his saucepan crown, and runs off with his tail between his legs. The storm blows on towards the forest.
The Ogre gives up. The Forest Ogre sits down with a bump and starts to cry. Then it stomps off home to its mum. The storm drifts on to the graveyard.
The Lich fades. With a long, sulky "Wooooo," the Lich fades into the mist. The candles flicker back on. The storm creeps up into the mountains.
The Ice Dragon flies away. The Ice Dragon shakes the snow off its wings and flies far away to sulk on a glacier. The storm sinks down into the mines.
The storm is over! The Fire Dragon dives into the lava and is gone. The green storm fizzles into a rainbow. The castle bell rings, and this time it rings for you!
The village of lanterns. Hollowbrook was a happy village. Every night, a hundred lanterns glowed along its streets, and the bakery smelled of warm bread.
Wings in the dark. Then one night, the Red Dragon came. It swooped over the rooftops and carried off the treasure, the food, and every last lantern.
The village in the dark. Morning came, but the village stayed sad and dim. The market was empty. Nobody sang at the inn any more.
The old training hall. Old Fern, the oldest person in Hollowbrook, found a rusty key. It opened the training hall, where the great masters once taught heroes.
A young hero. Someone stepped forward with a wooden sword and a brave heart. "I will learn," they said. "I will get our light back." That someone is you.
The road to the lair. Fight in the forest. Train with the masters. Grow strong. At the end of the road, the Red Dragon is waiting. Hollowbrook is counting on you!
Master Pip. In the training hall stands Master Pip: small, very serious, and holding a stick three times taller than Pip. "Lesson one," says Pip. "Never laugh at the stick."
Dame Wren. Dame Wren sits by the fire, sharpening her sword. "You're late," she says, "and your boots are muddy. Let's see if your sword arm is better than your manners."
Sir Tumble. Sir Tumble trips over his own feet on the way to meet you. Then he trips over a bucket. But when he lifts his sword, he never, ever loses.
Old Marrow. Old Marrow is older than the oldest tree in the forest. Nobody knows how old. He sips his tea, picks up his staff and smiles. "Ready when you are."
Madame Quill. Madame Quill unrolls a list of rules so long it reaches the floor. Rule one: bow. Rule two: no sulking. Rule three hundred: fight fair. "Shall we begin?"
Master Basalt. The ground shakes as Master Basalt walks in. His hands are as big as boulders, and his voice rumbles like gravel. "Go on, then," he says. "Hit me. If you can."
Lady Thistle. Lady Thistle waits in a garden of purple thistles. She smiles sweetly and offers you a cup of tea. Then she draws her sword. It is very, very sharp.
Captain Brisk. Captain Brisk checks his pocket watch. "Exactly on time. Good." He has never once been late, and never once been beaten. Today, you could change that.
Sage Ember. Sage Ember carries a little flame in his tall hat. He warms his hands on it while he talks. "Fire is a good friend," he says, "and a bad enemy."
Warden Stonefist. At the gate of the last road stands Warden Stonefist, as wide as the gate itself. He folds his huge arms. "Nobody passes without a fight," he growls. "Nobody."
High Master Orrin. On the mountain path, High Master Orrin waits beneath an old pine. "I am the last master," he says quietly. "Beat me, and only the dragon is left."
The smoking mountain. At the end of the road stands a black mountain, with smoke curling from its top. Deep inside, something big is snoring. The stolen lanterns glow in the dark.
Scorchtail wakes. A huge yellow eye opens. Scorchtail, the Red Dragon, uncurls from a mountain of gold. "Another little hero?" it rumbles. "Come on, then. Show me what you've got."
The dragon gives up. With a great huff of smoke, Scorchtail flops down. "Enough! You win," it grumbles. "Take your shiny things. I'm going back to sleep." And off it flies, far over the mountains.
The treasure comes home. You load the treasure, the food and every last lantern onto a cart. The long road home through the forest doesn't feel long at all.
The lights come back on. That night, Old Fern lights the first lantern. Then the next, and the next. Soon a hundred lanterns glow along the streets of Hollowbrook again.
The village cheers. The whole village pours into the square. They cheer your name, throw flowers and lift you up on their shoulders. The bakery hands out warm bread for everyone.
A gold star. Old Fern pins a gold star on your cloak. "A true hero of Hollowbrook," she says. "But heroes never stop training. Who knows what is waiting out there next?"
A dream. Every night, you look up at the stars and dream of one thing: a moon of your very own.
The old ship. In a dusty corner of the spaceport sits a small, scruffy ship. It is cheap, a bit rusty, and it is all yours.
Hello, Bolt! Inside, a little robot blinks awake. "Hello, Captain! I am Bolt. I know every planet out there. Shall we fly?"
Buy cheap, sell dear. Food is cheap on farm worlds. Machines are cheap where the factories are. Buy where it is cheap and sell where it is dear.
Watch out. Space has pirates and floating junk. A clever captain can talk, trade, run, or fight their way past.
Your moon is waiting. Save up enough credits, and a real moon will have your name on it. Fuel up, Captain. The stars are waiting!
